section_summary: This section contains consular despatches from the American Consulate in Dairen (Stuart E. Grummon and Troy L. Perkins) to the American Embassy in Tokyo, along with Department of State Far Eastern Affairs memoranda, detailing the implementation of the Manchukuo Petroleum Monopoly and the operations of the Manshu Sekiyu refinery at Kanseishi between May 1935 and December 1937. The correspondence documents crude oil shipments from California, Bahrein, and Europe, refinery construction, exploratory drilling at Chalainor, market supply stringencies, and separate commercial agreements made by The Texas Company in breaking the united front of foreign oil firms. Additionally, the records cover negotiations regarding indemnity for dispossessed foreign oil companies, Soviet intelligence inquiries regarding the aerial vulnerability of Dairen oil installations, and an unrelated misfiled consular report from Montevideo, Uruguay, containing agricultural statistics for the 1937 Foreign Commerce Yearbook.

subfiles.about: Report on the implementation of the Manchukuo Oil Monopoly in Dairen, regulatory controls on petroleum shipments, and operations of the Dairen oil refinery.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports on regulations enforcing the Manchukuo Oil Monopoly in the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone, including customs restrictions and police permit procedures. The newly established Manshu Sekiyu refinery at Kanseishi received crude oil shipments from California and solicited tenders for additional supplies. An attached press clipping provides details on the refinery's capitalization, production targets, and Manchuria's historical petroleum import statistics.
subfiles.title: Recent Developments in Oil Situation in Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Supplemental report correcting crude oil arrival data and evaluating the production capacity and import estimates for the Dairen refinery.

subfiles.title: Recent Developments in the Oil Situation in Dairen
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Dairen Despatch on 1935 Activities of Dairen Refinery

subfiles.about: Comprehensive annual review of raw material imports, production statistics, operating efficiency, and yields at the Dairen oil refinery during 1935.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon analyzes the first full year of operations at the Manshu Sekiyu refinery, tabulating 86,282 tons of crude and distillate imports from California and recording monthly refined sales. He compares actual refinery output against theoretical yields, noting lower gasoline recovery and higher diesel production than anticipated. The report concludes that technical problems are being overcome as the refinery shifts to full capacity, subject to securing doubled crude petroleum supplies.
subfiles.title: Progress of the Dairen Refinery During Its First Year of Operation
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Confidential report on separate negotiations by The Texas Company with the Petroleum Monopoly and supply shortages facing the Dairen refinery.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Reports secret negotiations between The Texas Company and the Monopoly, acute regional petroleum shortages, and diversion of refinery products to the Japanese Army.
subfiles.title: Reported Change in Attitude of The Texas Company Toward Monopoly and Difficulties of Monopoly in Obtaining Supplies
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Report on expanding operations at the Dairen refinery, corporate capital increase, shale oil improvements, and tanker shipments.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports that the Dairen refinery has accumulated abundant crude stocks, resulting in temporary storage congestion and exploration of export markets in North China. Manshu Sekiyu doubled its capitalization to ten million yen and invested in a coal hydrogenation plant at Ssupingkai, while exploratory drilling at Chalainor reached 917 meters without finding oil. An attached enclosure itemizes thirteen petroleum shipments received by the refinery during 1936 from California, Japan, Persia, and Romania.
subfiles.title: Recent Developments in Petroleum Situation
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Misfiled consular report transmitting supplementary statistical data on Uruguayan agricultural production, postal traffic, and population for the 1937 Foreign Commerce Yearbook.
subfiles.from: Leslie E. Reed, American Consul General, Montevideo
subfiles.summary: Transmits supplementary statistical data on Uruguayan agricultural crop production, postal communications, and estimated population for the 1937 Foreign Commerce Yearbook.
subfiles.title: Additional Information for Foreign Commerce Yearbook 1937

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Consul Grummon's report on crude oil shortages, Texas Company sales, and compensation negotiations in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Department memorandum reviewing crude stringency in Manchuria, Texas Company sales, failure to find oil at Chalainor, and Manchukuo conditions for company compensation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Dairen Despatch Concerning Petroleum Situation in Manchuria

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report on severe crude oil stringency, the Caltex alliance, refinery plant expansions, futile Chalainor drilling, and indemnity negotiations with Manchukuo authorities.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Consul Grummon reports on renewed petroleum shortages in Manchuria, noting that the newly formed California-Texas Oil Company broke solidarity with other Western firms to supply the Monopoly and Dairen refinery with crude and kerosene. The refinery completed additional storage tanks and a cracking plant, while exploratory drilling at Chalainor stalled in hard rock and oil shale development was planned at Sansing. Japanese officials in Hsinking reiterated refusal to compensate foreign oil companies for good-will, tying any compensation to long-term supply agreements. Attached tables detail tanker imports, refinery stock levels, and regional sales.
subfiles.title: Recent Developments in the Petroleum Situation
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Consul Grummon's report on inquiries by the Soviet Consul concerning Dairen oil facilities.
subfiles.summary: Department memorandum noting Soviet consular inquiries regarding Dairen oil tank capacity and stocks, presumed for Soviet General Staff military assessments.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Soviet Inquiries on Dairen Oil Stocks and Tank Capacity

subfiles.about: Report on an official visit from the acting Soviet Consul seeking intelligence on Dairen petroleum stocks and tank capacity, suggesting potential aerial targeting.
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: Reports inquiries by the acting Soviet Consul into Dairen oil storage capacity, suspecting intelligence gathering for possible Soviet or Chinese aerial bombardment.
subfiles.title: Inquiries by Soviet Consul regarding Dairen Oil Storage and Refinery
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
